texts.title: Oresteia I: Agamemnon
texts.subtitle: Ἀγαμέμνων
texts.author: Aeschylus
texts.description: Agamemnon comes home victorious from Troy, to Clytemnestra and her revenge. The first play of the Oresteia.

texts.title: Oresteia II: Libation Bearers
texts.subtitle: Choephori
texts.author: Aeschylus
texts.description: Orestes returns from exile and, urged on by his sister Electra, avenges his father on Clytemnestra. The second play of the Oresteia.

texts.title: Oresteia III: Eumenides
texts.subtitle: The Kindly Ones
texts.author: Aeschylus
texts.description: Pursued by the Furies, Orestes is tried at Athens before Athena's new court. The last play of the Oresteia.

texts.title: Persians
texts.subtitle: Πέρσαι
texts.author: Aeschylus
texts.description: The Persian court hears of the defeat at Salamis: the oldest surviving Greek play (472 BC).

texts.title: Prometheus Bound
texts.subtitle: Προμηθεὺς Δεσμώτης
texts.author: Aeschylus
texts.description: Prometheus, chained to a rock for giving fire to mankind, defies Zeus.

texts.title: Birds
texts.subtitle: Ὄρνιθες
texts.author: Aristophanes
texts.description: Two Athenians persuade the birds to build Cloudcuckooland between heaven and earth. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Clouds
texts.subtitle: Νεφέλαι
texts.author: Aristophanes
texts.description: Strepsiades sends his son to Socrates' Thinkery to learn how to talk his way out of his debts. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Frogs
texts.subtitle: Βάτραχοι
texts.author: Aristophanes
texts.description: Dionysus goes down to Hades to bring back a great poet, and judges a contest between Aeschylus and Euripides. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Knights
texts.subtitle: Ἱππῆς
texts.author: Aristophanes
texts.description: A sausage-seller out-demagogues Cleon for the favour of old Demos. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Lysistrata
texts.subtitle: Λυσιστράτη
texts.author: Aristophanes
texts.description: The women of Greece go on strike to force their men to end the war. Explicit content.

texts.title: Peace
texts.subtitle: Εἰρήνη
texts.author: Aristophanes
texts.description: Trygaeus flies to heaven on a dung beetle to bring the goddess Peace back to Greece. Some explicit content.

texts.title: De Bello Civili
texts.subtitle: The Civil War
texts.author: Caesar
texts.description: Caesar's account of his war with Pompey and the Senate (49–48 BC), from the Rubicon to Pharsalus.

texts.title: De Bello Gallico
texts.subtitle: The Gallic War
texts.author: Caesar
texts.description: Caesar's own account of his conquest of Gaul (58–50 BC), from the Helvetii to Vercingetorix at Alesia.

texts.title: Carmina
texts.subtitle: Poems (complete)
texts.author: Catullus
texts.description: All of Catullus' poems: love and hate for Lesbia, friends and enemies, myth and invective. Some are sexually explicit.

texts.title: Ad Familiares
texts.subtitle: Letters to Friends
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's letters to friends, family and colleagues — Caesar, Pompey, Cato, Tiro — over twenty years.

texts.title: Ad Quintum Fratrem
texts.subtitle: Letters to his Brother Quintus
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's letters to his younger brother, including advice on governing the province of Asia.

texts.title: De Amicitia
texts.subtitle: On Friendship (Laelius)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: A dialogue on friendship, set just after the death of Scipio and voiced by his friend Laelius (44 BC).

texts.title: De Imperio Cn. Pompei
texts.subtitle: On Pompey's Command (Pro Lege Manilia)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's first political speech (66 BC), urging that Pompey be given command against Mithridates.

texts.title: De Officiis
texts.subtitle: On Duties
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's last philosophical work, written for his son: what is right, what is useful, and when they conflict.

texts.title: In Catilinam
texts.subtitle: Against Catiline (Speeches I–IV)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's four speeches of 63 BC exposing Catiline's conspiracy against the Republic.

texts.title: In Verrem
texts.subtitle: Against Verres
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's prosecution of Verres, governor of Sicily, for extortion (70 BC).

texts.title: Philippics
texts.subtitle: Against Mark Antony (Speeches I–XIV)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's fourteen speeches against Mark Antony (44–43 BC), the last fight for the Republic.

texts.title: Pro Archia
texts.subtitle: In Defence of the Poet Archias
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: A short, celebrated speech defending the poet Archias's citizenship, and the value of literature itself (62 BC).

texts.title: Pro Cluentio
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Aulus Cluentius
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's longest surviving defence speech: a murder trial full of family poisonings and bribed juries (66 BC).

texts.title: Pro Ligario
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Ligarius
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: A plea before Caesar himself for the Pompeian Ligarius (46 BC).

texts.title: Pro Marcello
texts.subtitle: On the Pardon of Marcellus
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero thanks Caesar for pardoning his old enemy Marcellus (46 BC): praise with an edge.

texts.title: Pro Milone
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Milo
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's defence of Milo for the killing of Clodius on the Appian Way (52 BC), in the version he published.

texts.title: Pro Murena
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Murena
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: A witty defence of the consul-elect Murena on a bribery charge, in the middle of the Catilinarian crisis (63 BC).

texts.title: Pro Rege Deiotaro
texts.subtitle: In Defence of King Deiotarus
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero defends the Galatian king Deiotarus, accused of plotting to murder Caesar (45 BC).

texts.title: Pro Roscio Amerino
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Sextus Roscius of Ameria
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's first great criminal case (80 BC): a son accused of parricide, and Sulla's freedman behind it.

texts.title: Pro Sestio
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Sestius
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's defence of Sestius, and his manifesto for the 'best men' of the Republic (56 BC).

texts.title: Bacchae
texts.subtitle: Βάκχαι
texts.author: Euripides
texts.description: Dionysus returns to Thebes, and King Pentheus, who denies him, is torn apart by the god's worshippers.

texts.title: Electra
texts.subtitle: Ἠλέκτρα
texts.author: Euripides
texts.description: Euripides' version of Orestes' revenge, with Electra married off to a poor farmer.

texts.title: Hippolytus
texts.subtitle: Ἱππόλυτος
texts.author: Euripides
texts.description: Phaedra's forbidden love for her stepson Hippolytus, and the destruction Aphrodite brings on them both.

texts.title: Medea
texts.subtitle: Μήδεια
texts.author: Euripides
texts.description: Abandoned by Jason in Corinth, Medea takes a terrible revenge.

texts.title: Orestes
texts.subtitle: Ὀρέστης
texts.author: Euripides
texts.description: After killing his mother, the sick and hunted Orestes faces death at the hands of Argos.

texts.title: Histories 1
texts.subtitle: Book 1
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: Croesus of Lydia and his meeting with Solon; the rise of Cyrus and the Persian Empire; Babylon.

texts.title: Histories 2
texts.subtitle: Book 2
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: Egypt: the Nile, the pyramids, the priests and the Pharaohs.

texts.title: Histories 3
texts.subtitle: Book 3
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: Cambyses' madness in Egypt; Polycrates of Samos; how Darius became king.

texts.title: Histories 4
texts.subtitle: Book 4
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: Darius invades Scythia; the peoples of Scythia and Libya.

texts.title: Histories 5
texts.subtitle: Book 5
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: The Ionian Revolt begins; Sparta and Athens in the late sixth century.

texts.title: Histories 6
texts.subtitle: Book 6
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: The end of the Ionian Revolt and the Battle of Marathon.

texts.title: Histories 7
texts.subtitle: Book 7
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: Xerxes' invasion of Greece and the stand at Thermopylae.

texts.title: Histories 8
texts.subtitle: Book 8
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: Artemisium and the naval victory at Salamis.

texts.title: Histories 9
texts.subtitle: Book 9
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.description: Plataea and Mycale: the end of the Persian invasion.

texts.title: Theogony
texts.subtitle: Θεογονία
texts.author: Hesiod
texts.description: The birth of the world and the gods, from Chaos to the reign of Zeus: Cronus, the Titans, Prometheus.

texts.title: Works and Days
texts.subtitle: Ἔργα καὶ Ἡμέραι
texts.author: Hesiod
texts.description: Advice to Hesiod's brother Perses on justice and hard work: Pandora, the five ages of man, the farmer's year.

texts.title: Iliad
texts.subtitle: Books 1–24
texts.author: Homer
texts.description: The wrath of Achilles: ten days in the tenth year of the Trojan War, from the quarrel with Agamemnon to the funeral of Hector.

texts.title: Odyssey
texts.subtitle: Books 1–24
texts.author: Homer
texts.description: Odysseus' ten-year journey home from Troy: the Cyclops, Circe, the Underworld, and the suitors waiting in Ithaca.

texts.title: Ars Poetica
texts.subtitle: The Art of Poetry
texts.author: Horace
texts.description: Horace's verse letter on writing poetry and drama, hugely influential on later criticism.

texts.title: Epistles
texts.subtitle: Epistulae, Books I–II
texts.author: Horace
texts.description: Verse letters to friends and patrons on philosophy, ambition and how to live.

texts.title: Odes
texts.subtitle: Carmina, Books I–IV
texts.author: Horace
texts.description: Horace's lyric poems: carpe diem, friendship, wine, love and the brevity of life.

texts.title: Satires
texts.subtitle: Sermones, Books I–II
texts.author: Horace
texts.description: Horace's conversational satires: the bore on the Sacred Way, the town and country mouse.

texts.title: Against the Sophists
texts.subtitle: Speech 13
texts.author: Isocrates
texts.description: Isocrates' short manifesto on what education in speaking can, and cannot, do.

texts.title: Evagoras
texts.subtitle: Speech 9
texts.author: Isocrates
texts.description: In praise of Evagoras, king of Salamis in Cyprus: the first prose speech in praise of a real person.

texts.title: Helen
texts.subtitle: Speech 10
texts.author: Isocrates
texts.description: An encomium of Helen of Troy, written in answer to Gorgias' famous defence of her.

texts.title: Panegyricus
texts.subtitle: Speech 4
texts.author: Isocrates
texts.description: Isocrates' great showpiece speech (380 BC): Athens' glories, and a call for the Greeks to unite against Persia.

texts.title: To Demonicus
texts.subtitle: Speech 1
texts.author: Isocrates
texts.description: Maxims on how a young man should live: a traditional first text in schools.

texts.title: Satires
texts.subtitle: Saturae 1–16
texts.author: Juvenal
texts.description: Juvenal's furious satires on Rome: the city's dangers, women, the vanity of human wishes. Some explicit content.

texts.title: De Mortibus Persecutorum
texts.subtitle: On the Deaths of the Persecutors
texts.author: Lactantius
texts.description: Lactantius' account of the Great Persecution under Diocletian and the grim ends of the emperors who persecuted Christians, down to Constantine (c. AD 315).

texts.title: Ab Urbe Condita 1
texts.subtitle: History of Rome, Book 1
texts.author: Livy
texts.description: The founding of Rome and the regal period, from Aeneas to the expulsion of Tarquin.

texts.title: Ab Urbe Condita 2
texts.subtitle: History of Rome, Book 2
texts.author: Livy
texts.description: The early Republic: Horatius at the bridge, Coriolanus, the secession of the plebs.

texts.title: Ab Urbe Condita 21
texts.subtitle: History of Rome, Book 21
texts.author: Livy
texts.description: The outbreak of the Second Punic War: Saguntum, and Hannibal's crossing of the Alps.

texts.title: Ab Urbe Condita 22
texts.subtitle: History of Rome, Book 22
texts.author: Livy
texts.description: Hannibal in Italy: Lake Trasimene, Fabius the Delayer, and the disaster at Cannae.

texts.title: On the Murder of Eratosthenes
texts.subtitle: Speech 1
texts.author: Lysias
texts.description: Euphiletus, on trial for killing his wife's lover, tells the jury how he caught him. Plain, lively Attic prose: the classic first text for students of Greek.

texts.title: Amores
texts.subtitle: Love Poems, Books I–III
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's first collection: witty love elegies to Corinna. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Ars Amatoria
texts.subtitle: The Art of Love, Books I–III
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's mock-didactic guide to seduction, the poem that helped get him exiled. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Epistulae ex Ponto
texts.subtitle: Letters from the Black Sea, Books I–IV
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's later letters from exile in Tomis, addressed by name to friends in Rome.

texts.title: Fasti
texts.subtitle: The Roman Calendar, Books I–VI
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's poem on the Roman calendar, January to June: festivals, myths and stars, day by day.

texts.title: Heroides
texts.subtitle: Letters of the Heroines
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Verse letters from mythical women to the men who left them: Penelope, Dido, Medea, Ariadne.

texts.title: Metamorphoses
texts.subtitle: Transformations, Books I–XV
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's epic of transformations, from Chaos to the deification of Caesar: Apollo and Daphne, Narcissus, Pyramus and Thisbe. (Kline's translation is in prose.)

texts.title: Remedia Amoris
texts.subtitle: Cures for Love
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: The sequel to the Ars Amatoria: how to fall out of love.

texts.title: Tristia
texts.subtitle: Sorrows, Books I–V
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Poems from exile on the Black Sea: the journey, the last night in Rome, and pleas for recall.

texts.title: Satyricon
texts.subtitle: Including the Cena Trimalchionis
texts.author: Petronius
texts.description: The surviving fragments of Petronius' comic novel, including Trimalchio's dinner party. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Fabulae
texts.subtitle: Fables (Books I–V and Appendix)
texts.author: Phaedrus
texts.description: Aesop's fables in Latin verse: the wolf and the lamb, the fox and the grapes. Short and simple, ideal for beginners.

texts.title: Apology
texts.subtitle: The Defence of Socrates
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Socrates' speech to the jury at his trial for impiety and corrupting the young (399 BC).

texts.title: Crito
texts.subtitle: Κρίτων
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: In prison awaiting death, Socrates explains to his friend Crito why he will not escape.

texts.title: Euthyphro
texts.subtitle: Εὐθύφρων
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: On his way to his trial, Socrates asks a priest prosecuting his own father what piety is.

texts.title: Gorgias
texts.subtitle: Γοργίας
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: What is rhetoric, and is power worth having without justice? Socrates against Gorgias, Polus and Callicles.

texts.title: Laws
texts.subtitle: Books 1–12
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Plato's last and longest work: three old men walking on Crete plan the laws of a new city.

texts.title: Meno
texts.subtitle: Μένων
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Can virtue be taught? Socrates leads a slave boy to a geometric proof, and argues that learning is recollection.

texts.title: Phaedo
texts.subtitle: Φαίδων
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Socrates' last conversation, on the immortality of the soul, and his death.

texts.title: Phaedrus
texts.subtitle: Φαῖδρος
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: By a stream outside Athens: speeches on love, the charioteer of the soul, and what makes good speaking and writing.

texts.title: Protagoras
texts.subtitle: Πρωταγόρας
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Socrates questions the famous sophist Protagoras: can virtue be taught, and is it one thing or many?

texts.title: Republic
texts.subtitle: Books 1–10
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: What is justice? Socrates builds an ideal city ruled by philosopher-kings: the Cave, the theory of Forms, the myth of Er.

texts.title: Symposium
texts.subtitle: The Drinking Party
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Speeches in praise of Love at Agathon's dinner party, from Aristophanes' split humans to Diotima's ladder of love, until a drunken Alcibiades bursts in.

texts.title: Epistulae
texts.subtitle: Letters, Books I–X
texts.author: Pliny the Younger
texts.description: Pliny's letters: Vesuvius and his uncle's death, a haunted house, his villas, and his correspondence with Trajan on the Christians.

texts.title: Agesilaus and Pompey
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Sparta's lame warrior-king, and Pompey the Great.

texts.title: Alcibiades and Coriolanus
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Two brilliant, wilful men who turned against their own cities.

texts.title: Alexander and Caesar
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Plutarch's most famous pair: Alexander the Great and Julius Caesar.

texts.title: Demetrius and Antony
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Two great men undone by their appetites: Demetrius the Besieger, and Antony with Cleopatra.

texts.title: Demosthenes and Cicero
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: The two greatest orators of Greece and Rome, and their struggles against Philip and Antony.

texts.title: Dion and Brutus
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Two students of Plato who struck at tyranny: Dion at Syracuse, Brutus at Rome.

texts.title: Lycurgus and Numa
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: The lawgivers: Lycurgus, who made Sparta, and Numa, Rome's peaceful second king.

texts.title: Nicias and Crassus
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: The rich commanders of two disastrous campaigns: Syracuse and Carrhae.

texts.title: Pericles and Fabius Maximus
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Pericles in Athens' golden age, and Fabius, the 'Delayer' who wore down Hannibal.

texts.title: Solon and Publicola
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Solon, poet and reformer of Athens, and Publicola, a founder of the Roman Republic.

texts.title: Themistocles and Camillus
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: The victor of Salamis, and the Roman who saved the city from the Gauls.

texts.title: Theseus and Romulus
texts.subtitle: Parallel Lives
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Athens' legendary founder-king beside Rome's: the Minotaur, the Amazons, the wolf and the twins.

texts.title: Elegies
texts.subtitle: Elegiae, Books I–IV
texts.author: Propertius
texts.description: Love elegies for Cynthia, and in Book IV, poems on Rome's origins. (Kline's translation is in prose.)

texts.title: Bellum Catilinae
texts.subtitle: The Conspiracy of Catiline
texts.author: Sallust
texts.description: Sallust's history of Catiline's conspiracy: the other side of Cicero's In Catilinam, with the speeches of Caesar and Cato.

texts.title: Bellum Iugurthinum
texts.subtitle: The Jugurthine War
texts.author: Sallust
texts.description: Sallust's account of Rome's war with the Numidian king Jugurtha, and the corruption it exposed at home.

texts.title: Ajax
texts.subtitle: Αἴας
texts.author: Sophocles
texts.description: Denied Achilles' armour, the hero Ajax is driven mad by Athena, and takes his own life.

texts.title: Antigone
texts.subtitle: Ἀντιγόνη
texts.author: Sophocles
texts.description: Antigone defies King Creon's decree to bury her brother, choosing the gods' law over the city's.

texts.title: Oedipus Tyrannus
texts.subtitle: Oedipus the King
texts.author: Sophocles
texts.description: Oedipus hunts for the killer of Laius, and discovers who he really is.

texts.title: Oedipus at Colonus
texts.subtitle: Οἰδίπους ἐπὶ Κολωνῷ
texts.author: Sophocles
texts.description: The old, blind Oedipus, led by Antigone, comes to Colonus near Athens to die.

texts.title: Philoctetes
texts.subtitle: Φιλοκτήτης
texts.author: Sophocles
texts.description: Odysseus and Neoptolemus must win the bow of Philoctetes, abandoned on Lemnos, to take Troy.

texts.title: Caligula
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 4: Caligula
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Caligula: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Augustus
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 2: Augustus
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Augustus: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Claudius
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 5: Claudius
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Claudius: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Iulius
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 1: Julius Caesar
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Julius Caesar: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Titus
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 11: Titus
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Titus: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Vespasianus
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 10: Vespasian
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Vespasian: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Domitianus
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 12: Domitian
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Domitian: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Galba
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 7: Galba
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Galba: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Nero
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 6: Nero
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Nero: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Otho
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 8: Otho
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Otho: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Tiberius
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 3: Tiberius
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Tiberius: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Vitellius
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 9: Vitellius
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Vitellius: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Agricola
texts.subtitle: The Life of Agricola
texts.author: Tacitus
texts.description: Tacitus' life of his father-in-law, the governor who completed the conquest of Britain.

texts.title: Annals
texts.subtitle: From the Death of Augustus
texts.author: Tacitus
texts.description: Rome under Tiberius, Claudius and Nero, in Tacitus' surviving books (1–6, 11–16).

texts.title: Germania
texts.subtitle: On the Origin and Situation of the Germans
texts.author: Tacitus
texts.description: Tacitus' ethnography of the Germanic peoples beyond the Rhine.

texts.title: Histories
texts.subtitle: The Year of the Four Emperors (Books I–V)
texts.author: Tacitus
texts.description: Civil war after Nero's death: Galba, Otho, Vitellius and the rise of Vespasian (AD 69–70).

texts.title: Peloponnesian War 1
texts.subtitle: Book 1
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.description: The causes of the war: early Greek history, Corcyra and Potidaea, Athens' rise to power.

texts.title: Peloponnesian War 2
texts.subtitle: Book 2
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.description: The war begins: Pericles' Funeral Oration, the plague at Athens, Pericles' death.

texts.title: Peloponnesian War 3
texts.subtitle: Book 3
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.description: The Mytilene debate, the fall of Plataea and civil war at Corcyra.

texts.title: Peloponnesian War 4
texts.subtitle: Book 4
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.description: Pylos and Sphacteria; Brasidas in the north; the battle of Delium.

texts.title: Peloponnesian War 5
texts.subtitle: Book 5
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.description: Amphipolis, the Peace of Nicias, Mantinea, and the Melian Dialogue.

texts.title: Peloponnesian War 6
texts.subtitle: Book 6
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.description: Athens launches the Sicilian Expedition; the recall of Alcibiades.

texts.title: Peloponnesian War 7
texts.subtitle: Book 7
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.description: Disaster at Syracuse: the destruction of the Athenian army and fleet.

texts.title: Peloponnesian War 8
texts.subtitle: Book 8
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.description: After Sicily: Persian gold, revolts among the allies, and the oligarchic coup of 411.

texts.title: Elegies
texts.subtitle: Books I–III, with Lygdamus and Sulpicia
texts.author: Tibullus
texts.description: Love elegies for Delia and Nemesis, and the poems of Sulpicia, the only female Roman poet whose work survives.

texts.title: Aeneid
texts.subtitle: The Aeneid (Books I–XII)
texts.author: Virgil
texts.description: Virgil's epic of Aeneas, from the fall of Troy to the founding of the Roman people.

texts.title: Eclogues
texts.subtitle: Bucolics
texts.author: Virgil
texts.description: Ten pastoral poems of shepherds, song contests and lost land, including the 'messianic' Fourth Eclogue.

texts.title: Georgics
texts.subtitle: Books I–IV
texts.author: Virgil
texts.description: Virgil's poem on farming, trees, livestock and bees, ending with Orpheus and Eurydice.

texts.title: Anabasis 1
texts.subtitle: Book 1
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Cyrus the Younger marches inland against his brother, the Persian king, and falls at Cunaxa.

texts.title: Anabasis 2
texts.subtitle: Book 2
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: The Greek generals are betrayed and murdered by Tissaphernes.

texts.title: Anabasis 3
texts.subtitle: Book 3
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Xenophon rallies the leaderless army, and the retreat north begins.

texts.title: Anabasis 4
texts.subtitle: Book 4
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Through the mountains of Kurdistan and the Armenian snows, to the sea: Thalatta! Thalatta!

texts.title: Anabasis 5
texts.subtitle: Book 5
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Along the Black Sea coast, among Greek colonies and hostile tribes.

texts.title: Anabasis 6
texts.subtitle: Book 6
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: The army splits, and fights its way west towards Byzantium.

texts.title: Anabasis 7
texts.subtitle: Book 7
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Mercenary service in Thrace under the prince Seuthes, and the army's end.

texts.title: Apology
texts.subtitle: The Defence of Socrates
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Xenophon's short account of why Socrates chose to defy the jury rather than plead for his life.

texts.title: Cyropaedia
texts.subtitle: The Education of Cyrus
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: A fictionalised life of Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian Empire, as a model of how to lead.

texts.title: Hellenica 1
texts.subtitle: Book 1
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: The last years of the Peloponnesian War, from 411 BC: Alcibiades' return and the trial of the generals.

texts.title: Hellenica 2
texts.subtitle: Book 2
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Aegospotami, the fall of Athens and the rule of the Thirty Tyrants.

texts.title: Hellenica 3
texts.subtitle: Book 3
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Sparta at war with Persia in Asia Minor; the beginning of the Corinthian War.

texts.title: Hellenica 4
texts.subtitle: Book 4
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Agesilaus in Asia and at Coronea; the Corinthian War.

texts.title: Hellenica 5
texts.subtitle: Book 5
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: The King's Peace, Sparta at its height, and the seizure of the Theban citadel.

texts.title: Hellenica 6
texts.subtitle: Book 6
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Thebes rises: the Spartan defeat at Leuctra (371 BC).

texts.title: Hellenica 7
texts.subtitle: Book 7
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Theban supremacy, ending with the battle of Mantinea (362 BC).

texts.title: Memorabilia
texts.subtitle: Recollections of Socrates
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Xenophon's defence of Socrates and his memories of Socrates' conversations, including the Choice of Heracles.

texts.title: Symposium
texts.subtitle: The Banquet
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Socrates at Callias' dinner party: jokes, a dancing girl, and a lighter conversation about love than Plato's.
